note: Track keys, step 5: moving from a key to its two neighbours on the circle, through a shared chord and the new key's 5th chord. The key is moves (any key): the two key-chords panels and both backing tracks follow it, their chords written as numerals and named in the text as chord tokens counted from the first key, and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same. Each section ends with a feel to reach.

exercise.title: Moving to the key next door
exercise.why: Two keys next to each other on the circle share four chords and differ by one note, so a shared chord followed by the new key's 5th chord carries the music from one home to the other.

cells.text:
The first row below is the chords of {{=key}} major, and the second row the chords of the key a 5th up, the next key round the circle. {{chord:I}}, {{chord:iii}}, {{chord:V}} and {{chord:vi}} are in both rows.
Press each of those four chords in the first row, then in the second: the chord is the same, and its numeral is new.
Practice until you can say each shared chord's numeral in both keys without looking.

Press Play below to start the backing track. It starts in {{=key}}, reaches {{chord:vi}}, a chord of both keys, and then plays {{chord:II7}}, the 5th chord of the new key, which holds the one note {{=key}} major lacks.
Listen for the bar where {{chord:V}} sounds like home, and call out "home" there.
Practice until you can call it with your eyes away from the chord boxes.

Press Play below to start the backing track: the other neighbour now. {{chord:I}} turns into {{chord:I7}}, the 5th chord of the key a 5th down, and the backing track lands on {{chord:IV}} and stays in that key for four bars.
Look away from the chord boxes and call out "home" when the new home arrives, then look to check.
The new key is the other neighbour, and the chord before it is still its 5th chord.
{{?key}}In another key the chords have other names, and the two neighbours are still a 5th up and a 5th down.
